clue.text: Devastator of place and time

parts.note: locus is Latin for place, used in English for a site or position

explanation.surface: Something that lays waste to both a place and an era.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarms of these insects strip crops bare, so the insect is a classic ravager of fields.

clue.text: With cost adjusted price is about right without tax

indicators.note: the letters of cost are adjusted, that is set into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for price goes about, around, the letter for right

parts.note: a fee is a price charged

explanation.surface: Once the cost is adjusted, the price comes out about right and free of tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'is' are only links; a scot was an old tax, which is why escaping it gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a scot was a tax, so going free of it meant escaping payment entirely.

clue.text: Dive with breathing apparatus during exercise

indicators.note: during places the breathing apparatus within the stretch of exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a lung is the body's own breathing apparatus

explanation.surface: A diver plunging in while using scuba gear as part of a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing apparatus' suggests scuba gear, but it is the organ in your chest.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to dive headlong into water, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pet with pal struggling over a tree

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet

indicators.note: struggling suggests letters thrashing about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pet and its friend scrambling up over a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges PAL into LPA, set after the A it is 'over' in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The catalpa is an ornamental tree with big heart-shaped leaves and long bean-like pods.

clue.text: Endless malaise treated with sausage

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked
endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lingering unease cured by eating sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims MALAISE to MALAIS; 'treated' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, spiced Italian sausage.

clue.text: Music Leo composed for the theatre

indicators.note: composed fits the musical surface while saying the letters are put together afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece written by a musician called Leo for performance on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Coliseum is a large theatre, home of English National Opera.

clue.text: God rejected dissipated local rector at first — he gets it in the neck

definitions.text: he gets it in the neck

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of rector

explanation.surface: A rector who has turned from God and drinks in the pub gets his comeuppance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'gets it in the neck', being punished, while a clergyman literally wears 'it' round his neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's white collar is worn at the neck, so the cleric receives it there.

clue.text: Restaurant for the Greens?

definitions.meaning: the restaurant at the famous London hotel on the Strand
greens are leafy vegetables, and one variety is a crinkly cabbage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' looks like the political party but means vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The Savoy is a grand London hotel with a celebrated restaurant, and a savoy is a wrinkled cabbage.

clue.text: Newly arrived Scot became Emperor once

parts.note: something that has just come in is newly arrived
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman who had only just turned up went on to become an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Justinian I was a sixth-century Byzantine ruler famed for his legal code.

clue.text: Degree so elementary

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
sic is Latin for thus or so, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A degree that is so simple it is child's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and elementary both mean fundamental or simple.

clue.text: Tina's famous wedding location

parts.note: split the word as Tin a's: a tin is a can, then the letter A, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A singer called Tina recalls where her celebrated marriage took place.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Tina's' as 'Tin a is': a tin is a can.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel of John, the marriage feast where water was turned into wine was held at this Galilean town.

clue.text: Writer enters composition

indicators.note: composition means a putting together, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author takes up a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century novelist who wrote Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Harpies contrived to take a point from a self-righteous type

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Mythical winged monsters scheme to rob someone sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharisees in the Gospels are portrayed as hypocritically pious, so the word now means a sanctimonious person.

clue.text: Fast mover short of four feet — look out!

indicators.note: out here means outside: the word for look lies outside the measure

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily
an ell, an old English cloth measure of 45 inches, falls just short of 48 inches

explanation.surface: Someone without much height shouting a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: An ell is an obsolete length unit; 'out' has GAZE go outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The gazelle is a slender antelope famed for its speed.

clue.text: Wormwood makes thin base

indicators.note: makes signals that the following letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bitter herb produces a weak foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is both a name for the wormwood plant and the spirit flavoured with it.

clue.text: Narrow way for the donkey in Provence

parts.note: the French for the is l' before a vowel
âne is French for donkey, Provence being a region of France

explanation.surface: A tight track for a donkey in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as French: l'âne, the donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane is a narrow road or path.

clue.text: Mother retains headgear for the holy man

indicators.note: retains means holds within, so the word for mother wraps around

parts.note: mama is a familiar word for mother
a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: Mum keeps a hat on for the saint's visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian honorific meaning great soul, given to revered sages such as Gandhi.

clue.text: A soft little craving

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for soft
petite means small or dainty

explanation.surface: A gentle, small desire.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite is a desire or hunger for something.

clue.text: Nonsense writer, first name shortened with 25

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat
Lear's first name Edward has the short form Ned

explanation.surface: A whimsical poet whose forename was cut short is also a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with 25' points at 25 across, scholarship: someone having it is well-read.
explanation.definitionFit: A person possessed of scholarship is described as erudite or well read.

clue.text: Gents are unlikely to break up a relationship

indicators.note: unlikely signals an improbable arrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Men are not the type to call off a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to alienate them from each other, ending closeness.

clue.text: Regret taking root

definitions.meaning: to feel sorry for a sin
in botany the adjective describes a stem creeping along the ground and rooting as it goes

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to feel remorse, and the botanical adjective means creeping and rooting.

clue.text: Composer called an unfortunate, lacking ancestry

indicators.note: called means spoken, so the composer's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Carl Orff composed Carmina Burana

explanation.surface: A musician summoned a luckless person with no forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphan is a child without living parents, a sad figure cut off from family.

clue.text: Loader when working finds it a great trial

indicators.note: when working suggests the letters are set to work in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A labourer on the job finds it very hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or testing experience, historically a trial by suffering.

clue.text: Directors at sea?

definitions.meaning: a company's directors form a board, read here as a board

explanation.definitionFit: Directors together make up a board, and on board a vessel at sea one is aboard.

clue.text: Shoot a bird

definitions.meaning: a long-billed wading bird of marshes

explanation.definitionFit: To snipe is to shoot from hiding, and the snipe is a wader; shooting it gave the verb.

clue.text: Form of publication about sport shows scholarship

indicators.note: about means around, so the publication word wraps the sport

parts.note: an edition is one form or issue in which a work is published
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A version of a book on games shows learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep learning acquired by study, the same as scholarship.

clue.text: At the local one finds means of communication

parts.note: PH, public house, is the pub, a Briton's local
taken as written

explanation.surface: At the pub one finds a way to keep in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub; PH marks a public house on maps.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone is an everyday device for talking at a distance.

clue.text: Shop replacing gasometer?

indicators.note: replacing means placing again, so the letters are put back in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A big store built where the old gas holder stood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' rearranges GASOMETER, and also suggests a store built on its site.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastore is a very large retail shop.
